Title: From Test-Time Learning to Uncertainty-Aware Medical Foundation Models
Abstract: Modern medical AI systems are increasingly deployed in dynamic clinical environments where data distributions continuously shift across hospitals, scanners, patient populations, and evolving clinical practices. His talk will focus on test-time learning methods that enable models to adapt after deployment without requiring retraining or access to source data. He will further present recent work on uncertainty-aware medical foundation models, including conformal prediction techniques that provide rigorous confidence guarantees under distribution shift. Together, these approaches offer a path toward safer, more reliable, and clinically deployable AI systems for healthcare.
Biography: Associate Professor at Aarhus University and Founder and Director of the Adaptive and Agentic AI Lab (A3 Lab). He is an ELLIS Scholar, an AIAS Associate Fellow, and is affiliated with the Pioneer Centre for AI.His research focuses on trustworthy and adaptive AI for safety-critical applications, spanning test-time adaptation and updates, uncertainty quantification, multimodal foundation models, and medical image analysis. He has made contributions to self-supervised learning, open-set recognition, continual adaptation, and robust deployment of AI systems under distribution shift. He is the organizer of the 3rd Workshop on Test-Time Updates (TTU) at ICLR 2026 and serves in senior reviewing and area-chair roles for leading AI conferences, including NeurIPS, ICLR, ICML, CVPR, NeurIPS, and AAAI.

title: Behzad Bozorgtabar

content: Biography Assistant Professor in the Department of Computer Science at Khalifa University. He has previously worked as a Principal AI Scientist at Locai, and Inception Institute of Artificial Intelligence, Abu Dhabi, UAE. He obtained his Ph.D. from the National University of Singapore, worked as a post-doctoral research fellow at the ETH Zurich, Switzerland, and as a Research Staff Member at IBM Research Australia. Dwarikanath’s research interests are mainly in medical image analysis, machine learning, deep learning, decision support systems and computer aided diagnosis. He also explores other aspects of computer vision such as object detection and tracking, surveillance and image classification using deep neural networks. Dwarikanath has published more than 100 papers in prestigious conferences and journals, and holds 15 patents.
summary: Biography Assistant Professor in the Department of Computer Science at Khalifa University. He has previously worked as a Principal AI Scientist at Locai, and Inception Institute of Artificial Intelligence, Abu Dhabi, UAE.
title: Dwarikanath Mahapatra

content: Biography PhD candidate in the AIM for Health Lab, Department of Data Science and AI at Monash University. Her research focuses on computer vision, multi-modal learning, generative modelling, and explainable AI for medical image analysis. Her work spans latent diffusion models for controllable 3D image synthesis, vision-language model reasoning for interpretable diagnosis, and clinical decision support systems. She has published in venues including AJNR, IEEE ISBI, and ISMRM, and serves as a reviewer for MICCAI.
summary: Biography PhD candidate in the AIM for Health Lab, Department of Data Science and AI at Monash University. Her research focuses on computer vision, multi-modal learning, generative modelling, and explainable AI for medical image analysis.
title: Hongxi Yang

content: Biography Associate Professor of Computational Biology at MBZUAI,, Abu Dhabi, where he leads the Generative AI for Genomics and Medical Imaging (GenMI) Lab. His research focuses on human-centered artificial intelligence for healthcare, developing machine learning and multimodal AI methods to analyze complex biomedical data, including genomics, medical imaging, and electronic health records. His work spans both foundational and applied AI, addressing challenges in early disease diagnosis, prognosis modeling, precision medicine, and safe, robust AI systems for clinical environments. Before joining MBZUAI, he served as an Associate Professor in Human-Centered Machine Learning at the University of New South Wales (UNSW), Sydney. Prof. Razzak has secured over USD 15 million in competitive research funding, authored more than 250 peer-reviewed publications, and received best-paper recognitions at leading computer science venues. He serves on the editorial boards of major journals, including IEEE TNNLS, IEEE JBHI, and Neural Networks, and has chaired or co-chaired numerous international conferences, workshops, and special sessions.
summary: Biography Associate Professor of Computational Biology at MBZUAI,, Abu Dhabi, where he leads the Generative AI for Genomics and Medical Imaging (GenMI) Lab. His research focuses on human-centered artificial intelligence for healthcare, developing machine learning and multimodal AI methods to analyze complex biomedical data, including genomics, medical imaging, and electronic health records.
title: Imran Razzak

content: Biography PhD candidate at Monash University, working on medical AI and machine learning. His research focuses on test-time adaptation, domain generalization, and post-training alignment of large-scale vision, language, and multimodal models for robust real-world deployment. His work spans medical image segmentation, foundation model adaptation, and LLM post-training, with publications in venues including IEEE-TIP, IEEE-TMI, Medical Image Analysis, IEEE-JBHI, Neurocomputing, MICCAI, and IPMI. He also serves as a reviewer for leading journals and conferences, including IEEE-TPAMI, TMI, TIP and MICCAI.
summary: Biography PhD candidate at Monash University, working on medical AI and machine learning. His research focuses on test-time adaptation, domain generalization, and post-training alignment of large-scale vision, language, and multimodal models for robust real-world deployment.
title: Jianghao Wu

content:
Title: Towards Safer Medical AI Reasoning and Action
Abstract: Multimodal generative AI (GAI), particularly multimodal LLMs, is rapidly transforming the landscape of clinical AI. Yet translating this promise into real-world healthcare remains challenging, as model reliability and safety are tested by the complexity of clinical workflows, heterogeneous data, and diverse medical practices. In this talk, I will share our research on key limitations of current GAI systems, including skewed reasoning over multimodal clinical information, declining performance as clinical action spaces grow, and biases arising from regional diXerences in medical practice. I will also discuss our approaches to strengthening the safety and reliability of these AI systems in clinical decision-making and healthcare delivery.
Biography: an Assistant Professor of Personalized Medicine at MBZUAI. He received his Ph.D. from Imperial College London, UK, in 2023. His current research interests include medical foundation models, agents, and human-AI interactions. Some of his work has been published in leading journals such as NEJM AI, Nature Machine Intelligence, and The Lancet Digital Health. He serves as a guest editor for IEEE Journal of Biomedical and Health Informatics.

content: Biography PhD student in the Department of Data Science and AI at Monash University. Her research focuses on trustworthy medical image analysis, with specific interests in active learning, federated learning, and hallucination detection. She has published in top-tier venues including CVPR, MICCAI, and IEEE-JBHI, and actively serves as a reviewer for CVPR, ECCV, NeurIPS, MICCAI, and IJCV.

title: Jiayi Chen

content: Biography Research Associate at the University Hospital Bonn under the supervision of Prof. Dr. Shadi Albarqouni. He holds an M.Sc. in Biomedical Computing from TU Munich and completed his master’s thesis at the University Hospital Bonn and TU Munich under the same supervision. His master’s thesis focused on image quality transfer for ultra-low-field MRI, with particular emphasis on the Hyperfine SWOOP system. Previously, he completed his undergraduate studies in Electrical Engineering at Kuwait University and undertook a research internship at Sony Stuttgart as a deep learning researcher, where he worked on audio recognition and human avatar technologies. Currently, his research focuses on the use of medical imaging in radiation therapy (iMRT and VMAT), particularly for dose optimization and personalized treatment planning. In addition, he works on developing an AI service and its corresponding API as part of the OMI protocol.
summary: Biography Research Associate at the University Hospital Bonn under the supervision of Prof. Dr. Shadi Albarqouni. He holds an M.Sc. in Biomedical Computing from TU Munich and completed his master’s thesis at the University Hospital Bonn and TU Munich under the same supervision.
title: Malek Al Abed

content: Biography His research concerns the development of computational approaches capable of answering open questions in biomedicine and healthcare. He works closely with biologists, clinicians, and industry in problems of high relevance in both basic and clinical research, including: the development of automated methods for eye and systemic disease diagnosis in retinal scans (including the development of frontier retinal image foundation models) and the evaluation of AI systems supporting healthcare delivery in real clinical settings. He has co-organised a Institute of Physics workshop on “Microrheology and Transport in Complex Biological Media”, May 2022; The Alan Turing Institute workshop on “AI and data science in the age of COVID-19”, November 2020; workshops on cancer mathematical modelling at 13th and 14th World Congress in Computational Mechanics, 2018, 2021.
summary: Biography His research concerns the development of computational approaches capable of answering open questions in biomedicine and healthcare. title: Miguel O. Bernabeu

content: Biography Professor of Computational Medical Imaging Research and the Head of the Albarqouni Lab, his current research interests include Interpretable ML, Robustness, Uncertainty, and Federated Learning. His AggNet paper, published at the IEEE Transaction on Medical Imaging, was among the first ones on Medical Imaging with Deep Learning and has been featured as the top downloaded article for a couple of years at IEEEXplore. He has over 100 peer-reviewed publications in Medical Imaging Computing and Computer Vision, published in high-impact journals, and presented at top-tier conferences. His work is widely recognized, and he serves as a reviewer for prestigious journals, including IEEE TPAMI, MedIA, JBHI, and Pattern Recognition. Additionally, he reviews for major conferences such as ECCV, MICCAI, MIDL, BMVC, IPCAI, and ISBI. He has extensive experience organizing international workshops and conferences, including serving as Program Co-Chair for MIDL'22 and Organizing Committee Member for ISBI'22 and MICCAI'24. Beyond his academic pursuits, he is passionate about entrepreneurship and startups, particularly in developing innovative medical solutions for resource-limited settings.
summary: Biography Professor of Computational Medical Imaging Research and the Head of the Albarqouni Lab, his current research interests include Interpretable ML, Robustness, Uncertainty, and Federated Learning. His AggNet paper, published at the IEEE Transaction on Medical Imaging, was among the first ones on Medical Imaging with Deep Learning and has been featured as the top downloaded article for a couple of years at IEEEXplore.
title: Shadi Albarqouni

content: Biography PhD candidate in the Department of Data Science and AI at Monash University. Her research focuses on chain-of-thought reasoning for medical vision-language models. Her work spans on improving how these models reason through complex clinical problems and ensuring their outputs are both reliable and clinically meaningful.
summary: Biography PhD candidate in the Department of Data Science and AI at Monash University. Her research focuses on chain-of-thought reasoning for medical vision-language models. Her work spans on improving how these models reason through complex clinical problems and ensuring their outputs are both reliable and clinically meaningful.
title: Trang Pham

content: Biography Senior Lecturer and Deputy Head of the Data Science and AI Department at Monash University, and a co-founder of the AIM for Health Lab. Her interdisciplinary research focuses on developing computational methods for medical image analysis with technical emphasis on federated learning, disease diagnosis and prognosis models, test-time domain adaptation and trustworthy machine learning. In 2024-25 only, she contributed to several community service and leadership roles including: delivering 3 invited talks and 5+ guest lectures, serving on 20+ TPCs, acting as Editorial Board Member for the Journal of Intelligent Oncology, Local arrangement Co-Chair for the ACM International Conference on Multimedia 2024 (rank A*, >1600 delegates), Co-organiser of 2 workshops at ACM Multimedia 2024 and ACM Web Conference 2026, Website and Social Media Co-Chair for DICTA 2024, Special Session Chair at the 37th AJCAI 2024, and Session Chair for SHARE 2024. Her research work is recognised through several research publications and prestigious research grants totalling more than AUD $10m.
summary: Biography Senior Lecturer and Deputy Head of the Data Science and AI Department at Monash University, and a co-founder of the AIM for Health Lab. Her interdisciplinary research focuses on developing computational methods for medical image analysis with technical emphasis on federated learning, disease diagnosis and prognosis models, test-time domain adaptation and trustworthy machine learning.
